queue.recognise: You can recognise it by being the only tree on Argyle Street, an ash about 23 metres tall that rises above the tenement behind it. It stands in the small front garden strip outside 1223 Argyle Street, at Franklin Terrace.
queue.story:
The only tree on Argyle Street arrived by accident, in the roots of a primrose. In the 1850s the first residents of a new tenement at Franklin Terrace came back from holiday with primroses for their scrap of front garden, and an ash seed came with them in the soil. Nobody wrote down the year, so its age of roughly 175 years is counted from that story rather than from a ring.

By 1951, when James Cowan described it in From Glasgow's Treasure Chest, it stood 75 feet tall, about 23 metres, and had outgrown the building that planted it without meaning to.
